description: Somos los guardianes de la galaxia!!
summary:
APSIS is a space mission design simulator you play in the browser. In its first mission, FIREWATCH, one player or a crew of up to four builds, names, launches and operates their own wildfire-watch satellite, and learns why there is no single right design. Players assemble the satellite in 3D from real parts, choose instruments, a rocket and an orbit, then vote Go or No-Go as a crew. After the launch, they fly four days of operations, each role playing its own mini-game. What they chose decides what they can see: a thermal sensor sees heat at night but not through thick cloud. A final report traces the result back to their decisions, and they can redesign and fly again.

It answers the Space Mission Design Game challenge by linking objective, spacecraft, instruments, launcher, orbit, mass, power, data and budget in one loop, so players feel the trade-offs real mission teams face. Live NASA data is part of the game: real wildfires from EONET, VIIRS fire imagery from GIBS, ground stations from SSC, space weather from DONKI and the Deep Space Network, with links that invite players to read more.
details:
THE PROBLEM

A wildfire alert only helps if it arrives in time, and the satellites that send it are built from trade-offs: a better instrument adds mass, power, data and cost, and the orbit decides what you see and when. Students meet these ideas one at a time and rarely see their own choice come back to hit them three steps later.


WHAT YOU PLAY

Fire crews in Iberia need to know where a new fire starts before it spreads. You get one small satellite, a budget and four days to prove it can warn them in time.

  1. Design. Build and name your own satellite in 3D, or rebuild NASA's real Suomi NPP piece by piece. Then pick its instrument, rocket and orbit. Every part costs mass, power, data and money, and you will feel each one later.
  2. Go / No-Go. Four roles vote and the majority wins. The Mission Lab shows which check fails and the one change that fixes it.
  3. Launch and operate. Four days on a live map that also shows today's real wildfires. Each role plays its own mini-game.
  4. Report. See why the mission worked or failed, then redesign and fly again.


EVERY DECISION COMES BACK

A small battery fails a night pass. Coarse pointing gives false alarms. A slow radio delays the alert. There is no single right design, only trade-offs the crew must argue for.


ONE SIMULATOR, MANY MISSIONS

APSIS is the simulator; FIREWATCH is its first mission. Each mission is data in our .NET API's database: goal, budget, mass and power limits, eight phases, instruments and rockets. Roles, the Go/No-Go vote and the loop from design to report are shared, so the next mission reuses the whole game. Built with Next.js, React, Three.js, .NET, PostgreSQL and SignalR. NASA services are called only by our API, so no key reaches the browser.


HOW TO PLAYS

In the browser, nothing to install: solo with AI crew-mates, online rooms for up to four players, or offline.


LIMITS AND NEXT STEPS

The client and fires are fictional, and the figures are tuned for play, not engineering. FIREWATCH is the only mission so far. Next: more missions, difficulty levels and teacher tools.


TEAM

Zaragoza, Spain. Members appear in the members tab.

NASA does not endorse this project. No NASA logos are used.
